stewart_read: This is the classic hello-objection pattern but the rep skips the scripted small-ask ('30 seconds to explain why I'm calling') and instead free-styles into rapport.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be reading this as a warm re-engagement (customer previously inquired) rather than a cold no, which is plausible given 'we spoke to you a while back' framing.
coaching_implication: Use the protocol small-ask verbatim strategy on any first-30-second no, even on warm re-engagement leads, to create a clean commitment before free-talking.

stewart_read: Second timing deferral; rep asks a clarifying question but never re-offers a specific day/time before moving into verify questions.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be deliberately parking the time question to first build qualification rapport, planning to return to it after verify (which he does at 05:48) — but the return never lands a lock.
coaching_implication: When parking a time objection to run verify, explicitly say 'let's pin the day when we're done' so the customer expects to close the loop.

quote: if we were to get a food for it, is this something that can be paid monthly or... upfront complete you know, one the whole thing
stewart_read: Unsolicited financing question is a strong buying signal — customer is thinking about how to pay, not whether to engage.
coaching_implication: Rep answered adequately but should have used this heat to immediately push for the specific appointment time instead of letting the conversation drift to the text/email logistics next.

quote: I'm a probably have to let you know about that for sure because so many things come up sometimes all at once.
stewart_read: Third timing deferral lands right at button-up and the rep never re-anchors a specific fallback time or gets the 'is that fair' handshake.
coaching_implication: Should have offered two specific concrete times ('does Monday at 2 or Tuesday at 5 work better?') instead of asking customer to report back with availability.

stewart_read: Bill captured cleanly and rep reacts with mild acknowledgment but never flips it into alignment-against-the-utility language tied to the appointment.
coaching_implication: Flip should have landed here: 'so that $300 a month is basically funding the utility instead of your own system — that's exactly what the appointment is going to fix.'

quote: So we'll just plan on this. Just send me that utility bill as soon as you can.
stewart_read: Call ends with two open action items (bill send, time confirm) both owned by the customer, not the rep — no locked appointment exists.
coaching_implication: Rep should own the next step: propose a specific day/time and get a yes/no rather than asking the customer to initiate follow-up.
